correctness.rationale: For mixed v, any padding of ≥|v| zeroes preserves its standard occurrence count (including n=0 and the mandated leading-zero convention); bitwise complement then bijects occurrences. A fixed prefix adjustment for bar v produces one extra occurrence exactly when v is 1^r0^s; no other crossing occurrence can arise, so epsilon_v is independent of x. Reflecting the arithmetic progression about 2^K−1 in reversed index order preserves the positive difference d and introduces one common offset in all integer counts. This proves equality for every q, including infinite suprema. Independent integer checks cover 6,270 pattern/point cases and progression reversals, supplementing the proof.

final_claim: For every mixed binary pattern v, step d≥1 and modulus q≥2, the maximum monochromatic arithmetic-progression length for occurrence-count coloring of v equals that of its complement; exact reflection e_barv(2^K−1−x)=e_v(x)+epsilon_v holds with epsilon_v=1 iff v=1^r0^s and K sufficiently padded.
limitations: Mixed binary v only, standard specified leading-zero rule, integer nonnegative starts, positive steps, all q≥2; no constant-pattern or other-base result.
